evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong Multi-function Chinese Character Database)
evidence.field: 漢字甲骨部件分析; 形義通解
evidence.text: The database reads the oracle graph as a facial outline enclosing an eye and gives ‘face’ as its original sense. It reports that 面 itself is not attested in bronze inscriptions, though a related bronze graph uses 𦣻 plus an enclosure. It says a Chu-slip form’s enclosure changed toward 臼 and cites 面 ‘face toward’ in 上博楚竹書二《容成氏》簡14. These are database analyses and reported citations; the artifacts and slip text were not independently inspected here.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 面

evidence.source: 教育部《異體字字典》 (Taiwan Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants)
evidence.field: 說文釋形; 字樣說明; 注音
evidence.text: The entry gives the Shuowen account for 面: 顔前也, 从𦣻, 象人面形, and its Mandarin pronunciation miàn. It records 靣 as a variant spelling, but does not establish it as an ancestor of 面.
evidence.title: A04506 面 — Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: 教育部《異體字字典》 (Taiwan Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants)
evidence.field: 說文釋形; 字樣說明; 釋義
evidence.text: The entry says 麵 was written 麪 in Shuowen, glossed 麥末也 (Duan’s text: 麥屑末也), and analyzed as 麥 semantic plus 丏 phonetic. It says 麵 later became a common spelling and 玉篇 and 廣韻 equate 麵 with 麪. The entry lists later cited flour/food examples, including 後漢書 and 南史, but those citations do not date the first use of the word or the graph.
evidence.title: A04763 麵 — Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

gaps: No individual oracle-bone inscription for 面 was inspected or dated. The oracle graph and original face sense are reported from CUHK’s modern analysis; the Shuowen account is a historical lexicographic explanation, not independent confirmation of the graph’s earliest use.
CUHK reports no attested bronze graph for 面 itself, but the extent and limits of the database’s corpus were not checked.

The reported Chu-slip shape change toward 臼 and the ‘face toward’ use are cited by CUHK; the slip artifact and text were not independently inspected. Chronology and semantic links to ‘surface’, ‘side’, and ‘dimension’ remain unestablished here.

For 麵, sources support the older 麪 graph and its 麥 + 丏 analysis. They do not establish that the face word 面 was borrowed as the flour/noodle word, nor the exact chronology of 麪 to 麵 or separate earliest flour and noodle attestations. Do not infer borrowing from matching modern readings.

The local dossier’s Baxter–Sagart row for 面 and absence of a row for 麵 were not rechecked in this run; no reconstruction comparison is offered. The official Unihan records for 面 and 麵 could not be accessed, so current Mandarin readings lack verified upstream click-through evidence in this run.

Both Commons glyph candidates had failed acquisition in this run; their exact image URLs are therefore excluded. Search surfaced no independently verified alternate direct image asset. No Xiaoxuetang character query was completed, so no glyph image is proposed.
No source reuse terms were checked for recurring text datasets; this response recommends no local text extract.

limitations.text: The two exact Commons candidates established by description pages—the oracle redraw and Shuowen seal redraw—could not be fetched; their direct image requests failed. The unrelated Xiaoxuetang query supplied in the dossier returned HTTP 401, and no new per-character candidate was retrieved. Therefore no usable image candidate is proposed in this run.
